title: Inject secrets through the GUI
description:
Inject secrets through the GUI
    
Add a GUI option to append a DSB to the open file containing any
used TLS secrets from the session. The marks the file as having
unsaved changes.
    
Note #19128 - we don't currently have warning about saving a file
with a DSB in a format that doesn't support it, as we do with comments.
    
Fix #18400

Doing "Inject TLS Secrets" more than once will add multiple Decryption Secrets Blocks with the same content. Do we want to avoid this?

Yes, I think we do want to avoid it. The harder part is figuring out exactly how to avoid it.

There are workarounds for it, but they're not exactly satisfying: "Discard all Secrets" then "Inject TLS Secrets" (as long as you have the secrets in a key log file or you don't redissect before then), or if you worry about redissecting, "Export TLS Session Keys" to a key log file, "Discard All Secrets", configure the exported key log file, and "Inject TLS Secrets" again.

That's the same functionality as editcap (except that editcap can't extract #18197), but something a little more user-friendly would be nice.

What about adding an indication where each entry is fetched from (secrets block, separate file, derived from configured DTLS PSK, etc.), and only add a new block if not already fetched from or stored in a secrets block?

 capture comments depends on your file format. E.g., pcapng supports
 comments, pcap does not.
 
+|menu:Inject TLS Secrets[]                        ||
+Embeds the used TLS decryption secrets into the capture file, which lets
+TLS be decrypted without having the separate keylog file.
+Note that the ability to save decryption secrets depends on your file

+
+|menu:Discard All Secrets[]                   ||
+This will discard all embedded decryption secrets from the capture file.

commits_data.message:
Inject secrets through the GUI

Add a GUI option to append a DSB to the open file containing any
used TLS secrets from the session. The marks the file as having
unsaved changes.

Note #19128 - we don't currently have warning about saving a file
with a DSB in a format that doesn't support it, as we do with comments.

No longer export the RSA Session ID, only CLIENT_RANDOM related
information. This has been a long standing TODO.

Fix #18400
